title: Kiln quest chains (quests/*.json), format 1
description: A mod's quests, dialogue and quest NPCs, read by Kiln.Quests (managed/services/Kiln.Quests/Json.cs, System.Text.Json: comments and trailing commas allowed) and by the boot build of the game's journal, NPC menu and map markers (native/services/quests/questpack.cpp). A quest and a dialogue are in the game's own UI unless they say otherwise. Beyond the schema, kiln lint checks references across the mod's files: step ids, nodes, goto targets, givers, quests named by conditions and actions, and that the mod says "clients": "mod". Docs: docs/kiln/modding/quests.md.

knowledge.description: New knowledge objects of this mod: added to the game's GameKnowledgeResource at boot on the server and on clients with the mod (docs/kiln/services/npcs.md). Name them "<mod>:<name>" elsewhere, or by name inside this mod's native lines.

text.description: A string, or a text per language ({"en": "...", "de": "..."}; the game's language keys).

position.description: Metres: [x, y, z] or {"x": x, "y": y, "z": z}. x east, y up, z north.

near.description: What to search around: "player" (who gets there first), an id of npcs, or a place.

distance.description: Metres from what it is near: one number, or [min, max]. It widens by itself until a good spot is found.

site.description: A place found at run time: on real ground (the voxel surface), outside every base, not too steep; one per world.

margin.description: Metres to keep from a base's build zone (default 20).

inBase.description: A base is fine (never for enemies: the game pacifies them there and may remove them).

exact.description: Exactly at: no ground, no base check.

stepSpawn.description: Creatures the step brings into the world: on real ground outside every base, never saved, checked every second, spawned again when the game removes them, and after a restart or rejoin as many as are still owed.

tag.description: The Kiln.Spawn tag: a kill objective can name it.

level.description: The level to spawn at (0: the template's).

retries.description: How many times they come back when the game removes them (default 5). Then kiln.log has an error.

scope.description: world: shared progress. player (default): per character. both: a world object with a player twin (a player grant also sets the world's).

expectedFlags.description: Flags: the mask of flags that exist; a grant of another flag is dropped by the game.

npc.description: An NPC quests and dialogue refer to: a game NPC, or a new one (clone). In the world by itself, or put there by place.

dialogue.description: The conversation it opens (id of dialogues, or mod:id).

description.description: A roster NPC's line on the game's Survivors page: its summon tool's description.

place.description: Where Kiln puts it, on real ground and outside every base. It checks that the game keeps it there, and says so in kiln.log when not.

margin.description: Metres to keep from a base's build zone (default 20).

inBase.description: A base is fine: an NPC that belongs in one.

exact.description: Exactly at: no ground, no base check.

unlock.description: The game destroys a roster NPC whose unlock does not hold. true: grant it for this world before placing. false: wait until it holds. Default: true for a game NPC, false for a clone.

talkRange.description: How close a player must be to talk (metres, default 8).

clone.description: A new NPC: a copy of template under its own GUID (NpcId = FNV-1a of the GUID), one per world. true: GUID and name derived from the mod and this id. Needs "clients": "mod".

roster.description: An entry in the game's NPC roster (NpcCollection): the NPC directory, the unlock rule, recruiting and beds. Needs clone. At most 64 roster NPCs in all (the game's 35 included).

unlock.description: The knowledge that unlocks it: a name of this mod's knowledge, 0x..., or npc:<debugName>.unlock. None: always unlocked. Locked, the game destroys it.

workshop.description: An existing workshop's 0x id: its stock and crafting menu. Default: the base NPC's. A new id has no menu.

summonItem.description: The tool that places or moves it and sends it to a bed: an item's GUID, or an item definition (kiln.content's "add" entry: guid, name, base = an NPC tool item; "refs": {"equipment.placedEntity": <the clone's GUID>}). The game's Survivors list shows this item's name and description for the NPC, so a definition takes both from the NPC's names and description; say what the tool is in its caption or lore.

vendor.description: Its stock: kiln.content recipes ("add" entries), with station = its workshop's 0x id. A clone shares its base's workshop, so the stock shows at the base's NPC too.

giver.description: The NPC who offers it. A quest with a giver starts through that NPC, an action or code.

scope.description: player (default), party (players within partyRadius share credit, each gets rewards), world (one shared state).

auto.description: Starts by itself as soon as it is available.

retryable.description: Can start again after it failed or was given up (default true).

abandonable.description: Players may give it up (default true; never a world quest).

hidden.description: Not listed until it is active.

priority.description: Its order in the journal (the game uses 40..100; default 50).

journal.description: native (the default): the game's own journal, notifications and map markers; the mod says "clients": "mod", because clients build them from the mod's files. chat: chat lines and /quests, for a mod vanilla clients join, whom the game's UI cannot reach.

title.description: The step's short name in the journal; default its text.

voice.description: A voice-over line of the step in the journal.

marker.description: The step's map marker. A step with a place (site, spawn, a reach or kill place, an NPC to talk to or deliver to) has one by itself; this names it or moves it. false: none.

waypoint.description: Also write the player's waypoint, the game's own map and compass pin (default true).

name.description: The map marker's name; default the step's text.

base.description: The marker template to copy (default a search-area label).

spawn.description: Creatures the step brings into the world: one or a list.

objective.description: One of kill, collect, deliver, reach, talk, craft, build, knowledge, custom.
objective.x-kiln-message: an objective needs one of kill, collect, deliver, reach, talk, craft, build, knowledge, custom

kill.x-kiln-message: kill needs template, family or tag

countDestroyed.description: Kiln.Spawn destroying a match counts too.

to.description: The NPC who takes the items.

reach.x-kiln-message: reach needs at, offset, marker or site

site.description: The step's site is the place.

offset.description: From where the player stood when the step started.

marker.description: A template's name: the nearest entity of it is the place.

npc.description: An id of npcs, a template's name, or npc:<debugName>.

line.description: A dialogue line: line:..., 0x..., or <dialogue>.<node>.<option> of this mod.

node.description: A node of a chat conversation that must be reached.

knowledge.description: A knowledge name that must hold: npc:..., quest:..., query:..., line:..., 0x... .

custom.description: A signal's name (Quests.Signal, the signal action).

condition.description: One of knowledge, level, quest, step, item, predicate, all, any, not. Checked on the server.
condition.x-kiln-message: a condition needs one of knowledge, level, quest, step, item, predicate, all, any, not

is.description: Quest: locked, available, active, done, failed, started. Step: pending, active, done. Default done. Knowledge: true (the default) or false.

action.description: One of xp, item, take, knowledge, revoke, start, complete, fail, advance, reset, spawn, despawn, teleport, chat, toast, waypoint, talk, signal, call.
action.x-kiln-message: an action needs one of xp, item, take, knowledge, revoke, start, complete, fail, advance, reset, spawn, despawn, teleport, chat, toast, waypoint, talk, signal, call

xp.description: Experience through kiln.progression (as a quest reward).

value.description: knowledge: a counter's amount or a flag's number.

revoke.description: Clears that id only: what the game already did because of it stays.

flag.description: revoke: one flag of a Flags object (-1: all).

target.description: knowledge, revoke: default the player's object if the id has one, else the world's.

advance.description: quest or quest.step: finishes the current step (a deliver objective takes its items now).

offset.description: spawn, teleport, waypoint: from the player.

bindNpc.description: spawn: the entity becomes this NPC of npcs.

transient.description: spawn: never written to the save.

exact.description: spawn: exactly at the place given. Otherwise on real ground, outside every base.

despawn.description: Destroys the entities Kiln spawned with this tag.

toast.description: A chat line: Kiln has no toasts of its own any more. The game's notifications follow the journal.

waypoint.description: [x, y, z] sets the player's waypoint, false clears it, true with offset is relative to the player.

talk.description: Opens this dialogue as a chat conversation. The game's own menu opens only when a player talks to the NPC.

greet.description: The start node's text is a greeting. Default: true on a clone, false on a game NPC (its own greetings stay).

native.description: true (the default): lines in the game's own NPC menu, with the game's voice playback (needs "clients": "mod"): the start node's text is the greeting, each option a topic whose reply is the target node's text. false: a chat conversation through /talk, for a mod vanilla clients join. docs/kiln/services/npcs.md.

hint.description: The marker over the NPC's head on the greeting.

greetings.description: More greetings; shown before the plain one while their condition holds.

voice.description: A voice-over line, played by the game's dialogue: a name in the mod's cooked audio or a GUID of the game's.

hint.description: The marker over the NPC's head on this node's greeting.

goto.description: A chat conversation's node without options: where it goes on; "end" or none ends it.
The next node: its text is the reply, and its options join the NPC's topics from then on. "end" or none: nothing more.

reply.description: What the NPC answers; default the target node's text, else the option's own text.

voice.description: The reply's voice-over; default the target node's.

set.description: Knowledge the game itself sets when the line runs (at most 8 operations with the node gate).

once.description: The topic goes away once heard.

close.description: The NPC plays its outro after the reply.
